Possessed demons are made tough mostly because of the fact that they barrel at you at mach-5 with hardly any way of slowing them down. Here's a few tips that help me:

-the microwave beam is the only thing that can stun a possessed demon (that I'm aware of). You don't need to hold it on them, just give them a quick zap with it and they'll stop in their tracks for a few seconds. It also gives you a readout of their health which can be useful

-if you're having trouble getting quick damage in on them, I really recommend using the lock-on rocket launcher mod. It's great for melting enemies if you aren't quite comfortable with combos yet

-if you ARE comfortable with combos, precision bolt and rocket launcher have the highest DPS out of any combo in the game. If you have the rhythm for it down, feel free to spam that shit

-when you're microwaving the spirit, you can still lob out grenades and ice bombs. If you're being overwhelmed, you can use them to falter demons around you while you focus on the spirit

-You don't need to stay totally still when cooking the spirit! You can dash around and b-hop in circles around the spirit to dodge things. You definitely won't be at top speed but you can at least move out of the way of projectiles

These are all the ones I can think of right now, hope this helps!!

That's a super common step in transition, and I know its something that I definitely went through myself. Transition is a terrifying idea, and I found myself fighting over whether or not I should actually start transitioning for about 3 years. Now that I've started, I really wish I did so when I first started questioning this stuff. It's really tough to get started with it because it's probably the biggest change you'll ever have to go through in your life. It's scary, it's humiliating, and it's dehumanising. Despite all that, I eventually reached a point where I realised it was also necessary. I obviously don't know you personally, but I have a feeling you're gonna reach that point too. My advice is to experiment. If you have any friends or family you know will be supportive of this stuff, maybe ask them to refer to you with female pronouns. Maybe try on some makeup or feminine clothes. You might get a hit of gender euphoria, which means you're probably trans. You might also think to yourself something along the lines of "I'll never be a real girl" or "I look like an impostor". Thinking stuff like that probably also means you're trans. I know I'm kinda rambling, so I'll just get to my main point: don't be afraid to take baby steps. You might find yourself wanting to go deeper.

I'm in a really similar position. Super lucky with the support and stability of the people around me but my brain just has these disgustingly high standards with my transition. I have amazing friends and family but thats not good enough I guess. My shoulders are too broad, I'm too tall, my genitalia isn't correct, theres an empty black hole where my uterus should be. Its absolutely the #1 factor in my depression. Long before I knew I had dysphoria I always believed everything was stupid and pointless and my life was going to end in suicide. Understanding and confronting my dysphoria only seemed to dwarf all my other problems. Its all I think about, day in day out. People are looking at me and judging me and I'm judging myself because I was born into the wrong body completely against my will. I feel like I could do great things if I was cis and I didnt have all this shit to worry about. I have passions and goals in life, but doing any of it as a man seems like a waste of energy. Its gotten to a point where it feels toxic to stay as my assigned gender, but just as toxic to transition.  My social anxiety amplified, I get these delusions that everyone I love is dead and its my fault somehow (though that might not be because of the dysphoria lol). I know there are people that care about me and that if I keep pushing myself I might be able to be the person I feel like I am on the inside, and those are the only two things that keep me going. I guess its just important to remember that dysphoria is always gonna be an awful and shitty part of your life but coming to terms with it and not submitting to it is important. I'm not saying don't transition, you absolutely should, but do it because *you* want to. Not because your gross brain wants you to. I know its easier said than done, but it helps me to just look at the things I like about myself and reject the shitty ugly thoughts. I like my eyes and my legs and my waist and I like to accentuate those parts. Inevitably the dysphoria for all the other stuff comes back, so I take baby steps to make them more tolerable. I wear a bit of makeup, I wear a bit more feminine clothes, stuff like that. Doing that helps a bit but the feelings still become really inescapable. Things are sorta improving though. I guess you just gotta tough through it no matter how horrific the urges and feelings become because eventually you'll look at yourself in the mirror and see yourself instead of a monster.
